feed.title: Aadesh Ingle
feed.subtitle: Aadesh Ingle, founding engineer building production AI systems (agents, RAG, voice, evals). Writing on shipping reliable AI, deep learning, and the craft of engineering.

entry.title: Stop Being the Thing Inside the Loop
entry.summary: A production agent loop needs external checks, durable state, and hard limits. Without those, it is repeated prompting with a budget.

entry.title: Golden Cases Come From Funerals
entry.summary: Our golden cases are anonymized production failures with assertions attached. Keeping the original thread, trace, and expected behavior has made them more useful than cases invented before launch.

entry.title: The Model Is the Easy Part
entry.summary: In production, the model call sits inside permissions, policy, retries, evals, and traces. Those surrounding systems decide whether a promising demo survives contact with a customer workflow.

entry.title: The First Two Weeks Are for Listening
entry.summary: Before I build for a new client, I watch the people doing the work: their tabs, workarounds, retyping, and judgment calls. Those first two weeks often change what we build first.

entry.title: Evals Are the Operating System
entry.summary: A freight-negotiation agent had become too eager to close, and we could not measure the cost cleanly. An 87-test suite with 19 production cases gave us a release gate for the next model migration.

entry.title: The Bug Was in the Transcript
entry.summary: A voice-agent complaint can originate in speech recognition, model decisions, tool execution, or turn timing. I read the transcript and event trace in that order before touching the prompt.

entry.title: Trading Voice Quality for Reliability
entry.summary: A recruitment voice agent sounded natural but kept missing tool calls. We replaced one fused speech model with a slower, inspectable pipeline and measured whether reliability justified the extra latency.

entry.title: Three Thousand WhatsApp Messages a Day
entry.summary: A logistics customer receives about 3,000 WhatsApp messages and 500 emails a day. We turn them into CRM demand records with a queue, an LLM extractor, entity resolution, deduplication, and a review lane.

entry.title: Where the Human Belongs in the Loop
entry.summary: Reviewing every AI output wastes the attention human oversight is meant to provide. Route uncertain and irreversible cases to people, then keep their corrections as evaluation data.

entry.title: Writing Down What You Didn't Measure
entry.summary: I keep a small file of project claims beside the evidence for each one. It preserves the difference between a measured result, an estimate, and something we believe but have not tested.

entry.title: Demos Close Deals. Boring Systems Keep Them.
entry.summary: Ninety days after a successful AI demo, clients ask about failed batches, monthly cost, and recovery paths. Renewals depend on the answers.

entry.title: What Actually Happens When You Call an LLM API
entry.summary: An LLM request crosses rate limits, tokenization, scheduling, inference, streaming, and billing before your application sees a response. That fuller model makes 429s, latency drift, and surprising bills easier to debug.

entry.title: Running Two Model Providers in Production
entry.summary: We run OpenAI and Gemini across client deployments. Prompts need provider-specific work; the eval cases, contracts, and traces are what let us move safely between them.

entry.title: Own the Failure Before It Becomes a Story
entry.summary: After watching a friend write carefully about a breakup, I started treating personal failures more like postmortems: record what happened before memory makes my role smaller.

entry.title: Why Output Tokens Cost More Than Input
entry.summary: Output generation is sequential and keeps cached state in GPU memory while a response runs. That mechanism helps explain the price gap and changes how I set output limits, prompt order, and streaming.

entry.title: Principles I Reread Before Starting Anything New
entry.summary: Six notes I reread before a new project or commitment. Each comes from a decision that cost more than writing the rule down would have.

entry.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Cleaning Data
entry.summary: A logistics customer's transporter table had missing identifiers, aliases, and duplicate companies. Cleaning it improved the downstream systems that depended on those records.

entry.title: BLEU Lies
entry.summary: My image-captioning model scored ROUGE-L 39 and BLEU 10.3 on the same outputs. Reading the captions showed where both numbers were misleading.

entry.title: Search for Languages the Internet Forgot
entry.summary: My Master's work tested dense retrieval where training pairs, benchmarks, and web text were scarce. The hardest part was building evidence that retrieval worked in the target languages.
